headline: Last session: Sensex and Nifty ended lower as surging oil prices and FII selling led to weekly losses

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 26 October.

why: Brent crude oil prices surged to a six-month high, weighing on energy-sensitive Indian equities
Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) continued to dump Indian stocks for the 10th consecutive week
The market snapped a two-week winning streak amid profit booking and global macro uncertainty
Rising concerns over AI-driven cyber threats prompted security reviews of market infrastructure
whatHappening: The Sensex shed approximately 1,600 points during a turbulent trading week from October 19 to 23
Nifty 50 settled at the 22,600 mark while the Sensex fell 125 points in the final trading session
Kotak Mahindra Bank reported a strong Q2 with consolidated net profit rising 26% year-on-year
Jio IPO grey market signals suggest potential listing gains of over 22% ahead of its debut
summary: On the last trading day, Indian markets closed lower as the Sensex and Nifty succumbed to pressure from surging oil prices and persistent FII selling. Despite a mid-day attempt at a rebound led by IT stocks, the benchmarks ended the week with significant losses. Investors are now looking toward Monday's reopening while monitoring strong corporate earnings from lenders like Kotak Mahindra Bank.
